title: Crypto fraud complaints - which agency actually has jurisdiction
p1:
Lost money in a crypto scam? The first question many people ask is: “Where do I even report this?”

A surprising number of victims contact the wrong authority and lose valuable time while scammers move funds elsewhere.
p2: Many assume every crypto fraud case goes to one single agency. In reality, jurisdiction depends on what happened. A fake investment scheme, identity theft, hacking incident, or money laundering issue may involve different authorities.
p3:
For example, cybercrime reporting channels may handle digital fraud complaints, financial regulators may address certain investment-related misconduct, and law enforcement agencies may investigate criminal activity. The key step is documenting everything: wallet addresses, transaction IDs, messages, websites, and payment records before reporting.

The fastest response often comes from choosing the right agency and providing clear evidence.
conclusion: Have you ever wondered which agency should receive a crypto fraud complaint first, or have you seen someone report it to the wrong place?
